pages.title: Editor's Note
pages.text: Editor's Note Editor's Note This edition presents a focused, machine-assisted view of Northeast India during the configured coverage window. Rather than treating the region as a single narrative, the magazine organizes selected reporting into security, development, regional affairs, society and sport. The publication is produced through a reproducible pipeline that collects reporting, validates dates and content, evaluates Northeast relevance, ranks candidates, retrieves evidence and generates grounded editorial copy. The result is intended to make the selection logic visible alongside the stories themselves. 3

pages.title: Assam Rifles Seize Rs 5.07 Crore Heroin in Mizoram, Apprehend Two Myanmar Nationals
pages.text: Security & Strategic Affairs Assam Rifles Seize Rs 5.07 Crore Heroin in Mizoram, Apprehend Two Myanmar Nationals The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T06:59:55 In a significant operation targeting drug trafficking along the India-Myanmar border, the Assam Rifles seized 2.5 kg of heroin valued at approximately Rs 5.07 crore and apprehended two Myanmar nationals in Mizoram’s Champhai district. The operation was conducted at Zote, Champhai, based on specific intelligence gathered by the troops. Following the seizure, the narcotics and the arrested individuals were handed over to the Champhai Excise and Narcotics Department for further investigation and legal proceedings, as reported by a Defence spokesman. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/assam-rifles-seize-heroin-worth-rs-507-cr-in-mizoram-nab-two-myanmar-nationals-1619285 7

pages.title: Assam Rifles Seize Rs 5.07 Crore Heroin in Mizoram, Apprehend Two Myanmar Nationals
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Security & Strategic Affairs Assam Rifles Seize Rs 5.07 Crore Heroin in Mizoram, Apprehend Two Myanmar Nationals The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T06:59:55 This latest crackdown underscores the Assam Rifles’ ongoing efforts, in coordination with civil agencies, to combat drug-smuggling activities along the international border and safeguard the security of border populations. The operation follows a recent development in Mizoram, where the Excise and Narcotics Department destroyed seized drugs worth over Rs 11.82 crore at Bethani Multipurpose Farm in Aizawl. The disposal was carried out after courts concluded related cases, adhering to Section 51A of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985, and the NDPS (Seizure, Storage, Sampling and Disposal) Rules, 2022. The destroyed substances included 5.356 kg of heroin, 19.430 kg of ganja, 1.985 kg of methamphetamine tablets, 89.9 kg of codeine-based cough syrup, 0.418 kg of alprazolam, 0.04 kg of nitrazepam, and 6.830 kg of opium, with a combined estimated value of Rs 11,82,13,173. The seized drugs highlight the persistent challenge of narcotic smuggling in the region, with heroin and methamphetamine tablets—commonly referred to as Yaba or party tablets—being among the most trafficked substances. These drugs, along with codeine-based cough syrups, are frequently misused and illegally transported through clandestine routes. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/assam-rifles-seize-heroin-worth-rs-507-cr-in-mizoram-nab-two-myanmar-nationals-1619285 8

pages.title: Guwahati Railway Station Expands Capacity with Major Infrastructure Projects
pages.text: Development Guwahati Railway Station Expands Capacity with Major Infrastructure Projects The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T07:25:14 Guwahati Railway Station is currently managing over 50,000 passengers daily, with numbers rising to approximately 65,000 during peak seasons. This surge in passenger traffic has prompted the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) to accelerate infrastructure development projects across Guwahati and its surrounding areas. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/guwahati/guwahati-railway-station-handles-50000-daily-passengers-major-projects-under-way-1619287 10

images.alt: Guwahati Railway Station Expands Capacity with Major Infrastructure Projects

pages.title: Guwahati Railway Station Expands Capacity with Major Infrastructure Projects
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Development Guwahati Railway Station Expands Capacity with Major Infrastructure Projects The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T07:25:14 One of the key initiatives is the construction of the Kamakhya-Guwahati third line, a 5.74-kilometer project sanctioned at a cost of Rs 467 crore. Scheduled for completion by 2028, this additional line aims to increase capacity, reduce congestion, and improve train operations for passengers and residents of Kamrup Metro district. Another significant project is the Agthori-Kamakhya double line, which includes the second Saraighat Rail-cum-Road Bridge. The Rs 1,474 crore project spans 7.20 kilometers, featuring a 1.3-kilometer bridge that will carry a double-line railway track alongside a three-lane road. This infrastructure is expected to enhance rail and road connectivity across the Brahmaputra while easing pressure on the existing Saraighat Bridge. The development of a Mega Coaching Complex at New Guwahati is also underway, with a sanctioned cost of Rs 227 crore. This facility will bolster train terminal and maintenance capabilities in the region. Additionally, the redevelopment of Guwahati and Kamakhya railway stations is in progress, focusing on modern amenities and improved accessibility. Guwahati Railway Station is being transformed into a green-building facility, incorporating solar power, waste management, and water management systems. To address environmental and wildlife concerns, the Kamakhya-Azara Elevated Corridor is being constructed. This project includes an elevated viaduct along the stretch, including sections near Deepor Beel, to ensure safe wildlife movement while maintaining efficient rail connectivity. The remaining 13.25-kilometer Azara-Kamakhya double-line stretch is targeted for completion by July 2028. The NFR is also enhancing freight and logistics infrastructure through Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals. The GCT at Baihata, located near Guwahati, has already been completed, improving freight-handling and logistics operations in the region. These projects collectively aim to expand railway capacity, reduce congestion, and enhance the efficiency of train services around Guwahati. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/guwahati/guwahati-railway-station-handles-50000-daily-passengers-major-projects-under-way-1619287 11

pages.title: Assam CM Highlights Land Shortage as Key Industrial Hurdle; Govt Pushes for Land Banks and Estates
pages.text: Development Assam CM Highlights Land Shortage as Key Industrial Hurdle; Govt Pushes for Land Banks and Estates The Assam Tribune 2026-09-10T09:09:06 Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has identified the shortage of suitable land as a major barrier to industrial growth in the state, stating that many potential investors are unable to establish operations due to this constraint. Speaking at the inauguration of PepsiCo India’s Rs 787-crore food manufacturing plant in Banekuchi, Nalbari, Sarma emphasized the government’s proactive approach to address this issue by creating land banks and developing industrial estates at strategic locations. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/assam/land-crunch-hindering-assam-industry-says-cm-govt-plans-land-banks-estates-1616912 12

images.alt: Assam CM Highlights Land Shortage as Key Industrial Hurdle; Govt Pushes for Land Banks and Estates

pages.title: Assam CM Highlights Land Shortage as Key Industrial Hurdle; Govt Pushes for Land Banks and Estates
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Development Assam CM Highlights Land Shortage as Key Industrial Hurdle; Govt Pushes for Land Banks and Estates The Assam Tribune 2026-09-10T09:09:06 "We need land. Many industries want to come to Assam, but due to the absence of suitable land, they could not come. So, now we are trying to create land banks. Wherever there is land, we will take industries there," Sarma said, underlining the urgency of the situation. The focus, he added, is on identifying land near railway stations and highways to facilitate the establishment of industrial estates. "To create industrial estates, we need suitable land near railway stations and highways. Wherever we find land in such locations, we have decided to build industrial estates there," the Chief Minister stated, outlining the government’s strategy to enhance industrial infrastructure. The inauguration of the PepsiCo facility, which is expected to generate over 200 direct and 500 indirect employment opportunities—with around 75% of the workforce comprising women—marks a significant milestone for Assam’s industrial sector. Sarma highlighted that approximately 120 women will receive digital literacy training as part of the initiative. The project, which was laid out by Sarma and then Industries Minister Chandra Mohan Patowary on September 3, 2023, is poised to transform Assam’s manufacturing landscape, with products from the facility set to be distributed nationwide. The facility’s operations will also bolster local agriculture, particularly the potato sector. PepsiCo currently requires around 30,000 metric tonnes of potatoes annually, with projections indicating a rise to 70,000 metric tonnes by 2030. To support this demand, the state government, PepsiCo, and the State Bank of India have collaborated to facilitate the procurement of specialized potato seeds for farmers through Kisan Credit Cards, benefiting around 5,000 farmers and their families. Additionally, a Rs 35-crore cold storage facility with a capacity of 10,000 tonnes is being established to strengthen the potato supply chain. Sarma stressed the importance of expanding industries within Assam to reduce the state’s workforce dependence on employment opportunities outside the state. He cited the Shraddhanjali scheme, which has, in some months, brought back as many as 50 bodies of Assamese workers who died while working in other states, including Karnataka, Telangana, Maharashtra, and Kerala. "To prevent such situations, we need to establish industries and create employment opportunities within Assam so that our people do not have to leave the state in search of work," he said. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/assam/land-crunch-hindering-assam-industry-says-cm-govt-plans-land-banks-estates-1616912 13

pages.title: Mizoram Fails to Receive SASCI Funds in 2026-27, Opposition Demands Explanation from CM Lalduhoma
pages.text: Development Mizoram Fails to Receive SASCI Funds in 2026-27, Opposition Demands Explanation from CM Lalduhoma The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T05:49:20 The Mizoram Government has received no funds under the Centre’s Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) scheme during the current financial year, according to an RTI reply from the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance. The Opposition Mizo National Front (MNF) has cited this information in a press release, raising concerns over the state’s financial management under Chief Minister Pu Lalduhoma, who also holds the Finance portfolio. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/centre-funds-not-released-to-mizoram-mnf-seeks-explanation-from-cm-lalduhoma-1619278 15

images.alt: Mizoram Fails to Receive SASCI Funds in 2026-27, Opposition Demands Explanation from CM Lalduhoma

pages.title: Mizoram Fails to Receive SASCI Funds in 2026-27, Opposition Demands Explanation from CM Lalduhoma
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Development Mizoram Fails to Receive SASCI Funds in 2026-27, Opposition Demands Explanation from CM Lalduhoma The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T05:49:20 As of September 30, 2026, seven of the eight North Eastern States had received SASCI funds for 2026-27, while Mizoram received zero rupees. The allocations for other states were as follows: Arunachal Pradesh received Rs 3,965.82 crore, Nagaland Rs 3,324.68 crore, Tripura Rs 2,613.17 crore, Assam Rs 2,504.16 crore, Manipur Rs 2,129.24 crore, Meghalaya Rs 1,947.14 crore, and Sikkim Rs 921.97 crore. The SASCI scheme provides states with 50-year interest-free loans for capital investment projects, with the Union Government allocating Rs 2 lakh crore for 2026-27 under this scheme. The MNF highlighted that Mizoram has faced difficulties in availing SASCI funds since the Zoram People’s Movement (ZPM) Government took power in December 2023. The party alleged that Rs 233.31 crore sanctioned to Mizoram under SASCI in 2023-24 had lapsed, and another Rs 111.52 crore sanctioned in 2025-26 suffered the same fate. The Opposition attributed this to poor financial management by Chief Minister Lalduhoma and demanded an explanation from him in his capacity as both Chief Minister and Finance Minister. The MNF further alleged that the Mizoram Government had previously submitted utilisation certificates without releasing the corresponding SASCI funds. The party stated it would monitor the issue closely and take up any such matter with the Centre if similar instances occurred in the future. The Department of Expenditure, the Union Government’s nodal department for state finances, including the release of special assistance, was not directly quoted but referenced in the context of the RTI reply. The Opposition’s press release underscores the urgency of addressing the financial discrepancies, with the MNF insisting that the zero fund release for 2026-27 warrants a formal explanation from Lalduhoma. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/centre-funds-not-released-to-mizoram-mnf-seeks-explanation-from-cm-lalduhoma-1619278 16

pages.title: NEC Pledges Comprehensive Support to Nagaland’s Coffee Sector Amid Push for Modernization
pages.text: Development NEC Pledges Comprehensive Support to Nagaland’s Coffee Sector Amid Push for Modernization The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T05:36:04 The North Eastern Council (NEC) has reaffirmed its commitment to bolstering Nagaland’s coffee farming community, with Secretary Satinder Kumar Bhalla emphasizing the need for modernization and integrated development during a recent review of the Coffee USP Project in Tuophema village, Kohima district. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/nec-assures-support-to-nagaland-coffee-farmers-pushes-modernisation-1619276 17

images.alt: NEC Pledges Comprehensive Support to Nagaland’s Coffee Sector Amid Push for Modernization

pages.title: NEC Pledges Comprehensive Support to Nagaland’s Coffee Sector Amid Push for Modernization
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Development NEC Pledges Comprehensive Support to Nagaland’s Coffee Sector Amid Push for Modernization The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T05:36:04 During his visit, Bhalla inspected coffee plantation sites and the Hi-Tech Coffee Washing Station, engaging directly with local growers and cluster members. He underscored that the Coffee USP Project extends beyond mere plantation initiatives, framing it as an ‘integrated livelihood and economic development programme’ designed to maximize value from the region’s natural and human resources. Bhalla highlighted critical gaps hindering the sector’s competitiveness, stating that commercial viability requires ‘good road connectivity, modern processing machinery, efficient post-harvest infrastructure, quality assurance, value addition, and strong market and export linkages.’ He stressed that these improvements are essential for transforming coffee cultivation into a sustainable economic driver for rural communities. The NEC Secretary also urged the Nagaland Government and the Coffee Board to collaborate with Central agricultural institutions to identify suitable intercrops and complementary activities for coffee plantations. Such diversification, he noted, would enhance land productivity and provide farmers with additional income streams, thereby strengthening the sector’s economic resilience. Bhalla’s remarks followed a broader directive from North Eastern States’ Chief Ministers to devise strategies aimed at significantly boosting farmers’ incomes. He reiterated that achieving this goal demands coordinated efforts from the Government of India, Nagaland Government, Coffee Board, local administration, farmers, technical institutions, and the private sector. The visit concluded with Bhalla expressing optimism that the project would lead to a ‘substantial increase in the income of farmers and communities,’ contingent upon addressing challenges like water harvesting, mechanization, and technology adoption. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/nec-assures-support-to-nagaland-coffee-farmers-pushes-modernisation-1619276 18

pages.title: Final Campaign Day in Nagaon Bypoll: BJP, Congress, AIUDF Trade Barbs as Polls Near
pages.text: Regional News Final Campaign Day in Nagaon Bypoll: BJP, Congress, AIUDF Trade Barbs as Polls Near The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T12:21:04 The campaign for the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll concluded at 5 pm on Sunday, October 4, with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Indian National Congress (Congress), and All India United Democratic Front (AIUDF) making their last appeals to voters ahead of polling on October 6. Senior leaders from all three parties intensified their efforts as the constituency entered the mandatory 48-hour silence period, which began immediately after the campaign ended. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/assam/nagaon-bypoll-bjp-congress-aiudf-make-final-pitches-trade-barbs-as-campaign-ends-1619316 20

images.alt: Final Campaign Day in Nagaon Bypoll: BJP, Congress, AIUDF Trade Barbs as Polls Near

pages.title: Final Campaign Day in Nagaon Bypoll: BJP, Congress, AIUDF Trade Barbs as Polls Near
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Regional News Final Campaign Day in Nagaon Bypoll: BJP, Congress, AIUDF Trade Barbs as Polls Near The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T12:21:04 BJP leaders, including Assam Minister and party leader Pijush Hazarika, targeted AIUDF chief Maulana Badruddin Ajmal and Congress MLA Asif Mohammad Nazar during a rally in Lahorighat. Hazarika criticized Ajmal’s health, describing him as "an ailing man" who "would not be able to work without assistance." He urged Ajmal to stop campaigning and seek treatment in Dubai, stating, "He has to be supported and helped by two people." The BJP’s campaign also saw participation from state president Dilip Saikia and Finance Minister Jayanta Mallabaruah, who addressed supporters in Raha. Saikia emphasized voter confidence in the BJP, declaring, "People support BJP because they know the things that the party has been doing for them." He further urged voters to support Devasish Sharma for the bypolls, as supporters chanted in unison. The Congress held campaign meetings in Lahorighat and Raha, rallying behind candidate Sibamoni Bora. APCC president Gaurav Gogoi, AICC secretary Manoj Chauhan, and MLAs Asif Mohammad Nazar and Baby Begum attended the gatherings, which the party described as reflecting its focus on "unity, harmony, democracy, and development." Gogoi directed sharp criticism at AIUDF and Ajmal, alleging a close political alliance between Ajmal and Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma. He claimed Ajmal had functioned as the BJP’s "B Team" and predicted that the AIUDF would cease to exist after the bypolls, with Sarma eventually inducting Ajmal into the BJP. Gogoi stated, "Maulana Badruddin Ajmal is the closest friend of Himanta Biswa Sarma in Assam politics." The Nagaon bypoll was triggered by the resignation of former Congress MP Pradyut Bordoloi from the Lok Sabha seat, who later won the Dispur Assembly seat on a BJP ticket. With campaigning now over, the constituency observes the silence period until polling day on October 6, with counting scheduled for October 9. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/assam/nagaon-bypoll-bjp-congress-aiudf-make-final-pitches-trade-barbs-as-campaign-ends-1619316 21

pages.title: Search Suspended After 71-Year-Old Man Found Dead in Manipur’s Kangpokpi Forest
pages.text: Regional News Search Suspended After 71-Year-Old Man Found Dead in Manipur’s Kangpokpi Forest The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T12:00:08 A 71-year-old man identified as Hemjang Haokip was found dead in a forest near Manipur’s Kangpokpi district on Sunday, following his disappearance after an incident involving his field hut. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/missing-71-year-old-kuki-man-found-dead-in-manipurs-kangpokpi-forest-1619314 22

images.alt: Search Suspended After 71-Year-Old Man Found Dead in Manipur’s Kangpokpi Forest

pages.title: Search Suspended After 71-Year-Old Man Found Dead in Manipur’s Kangpokpi Forest
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Regional News Search Suspended After 71-Year-Old Man Found Dead in Manipur’s Kangpokpi Forest The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T12:00:08 Haokip, a resident of Khunkho Kuki Village near Leimakhong, had gone missing after his field hut was allegedly set ablaze on Saturday. His body was later discovered with his hands reportedly tied behind his back, according to sources. His farm trousers, shirt, and sweater were recovered during a search operation on Sunday, which involved the deployment of sniffer dogs and intensified efforts by security forces. The search for Haokip began after villagers noticed his hut was burnt and he was missing. Heavy rainfall on Saturday had kept many villagers away from their fields, and the incident came to light only in the evening. Haokip was known to spend nights in his field hut. Despite a search that continued until dark, he could not be located, and the operation was suspended due to darkness and security concerns. The Kuki Youth Organisation (KYO), Leimakhong Block, had earlier called for Haokip’s immediate and safe return, urging authorities and security agencies to intensify the search and take action against those responsible. Meanwhile, the Ariang (Khunkhu) Naga Village Authority issued a clarification, stating that their village and residents had no involvement in Haokip’s disappearance. The authority emphasized that the two villages had maintained peaceful and cordial relations for decades and appealed against unverified allegations, warning that such claims could create unnecessary distrust and tension. The village authority also mentioned that movement restrictions had been imposed on its residents from August 14 as a precautionary measure following an earlier incident involving Naga villages. The incident involving Haokip’s disappearance and death occurs amid renewed tensions between Kuki and Naga communities in Manipur, particularly in Kangpokpi and neighboring areas, where reports of abductions, hostage-taking, and attacks involving civilians have been reported in recent months. Security forces continued search and security operations in the area, but further details surrounding Haokip’s death remain awaited. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/north-east/missing-71-year-old-kuki-man-found-dead-in-manipurs-kangpokpi-forest-1619314 23

pages.title: Nagaon Bypoll: Alleged Pushback of Women Sparks Political Debate
pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Society & Youth Nagaon Bypoll: Alleged Pushback of Women Sparks Political Debate The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T09:38:43 Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi has written to Union External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, seeking urgent action to trace and bring back Jahanara Begum of Bagariguri and Mumtaz Begum of Dhing Gaon. According to Gogoi’s letter dated October 2, the two women were allegedly sent across the India-Bangladesh border through Gate No. 2 near Border Pillar No. 1339/MP during the night of June 13–14, 2026. Their whereabouts remain unknown since then. The case stems from Foreigners Tribunal proceedings in Nagaon, where both women were declared foreigners in 2019. They challenged the tribunal’s decisions in the Gauhati High Court, which in April 2026 set aside the earlier opinions and remanded the cases for fresh consideration due to insufficient material evidence, as per Gogoi’s letter. Following the High Court’s directions, Jahanara appeared before the tribunal on May 29, and Mumtaz on May 30. Gogoi alleged that both women were taken into custody shortly afterward, preventing them from obtaining fresh tribunal opinions or challenging them in court. The Gauhati High Court later observed that the tribunal office had ‘deliberately and wilfully delayed’ issuing a certified copy of its opinion in Mumtaz’s case, ruling that the state machinery had obstructed her right to approach the High Court. Similar findings were recorded in Jahanara’s case, with the court also describing the June 2 expulsion orders—directing the women to leave India within 24 hours—as ‘farcical’. The High Court directed the Ministry of External Affairs to locate the women in Bangladesh and facilitate their return to India for legal recourse. Meanwhile, the case has become entangled in the bypoll campaign, with Mumtaz’s son appealing to political parties to prioritize finding her rather than politicizing the issue. He urged both the Congress and AIUDF to assist in tracing her, stating, ‘We want to find her, where is she,’ and expressed a desire to meet Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and BJP’s Nagaon candidate Devashish Sharma, who was the District Commissioner when the expulsion order was issued. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/assam/nagaon-bypoll-womens-alleged-pushback-to-bangladesh-fuels-political-sparring-1619301 26

pages.title: Roaming cattle and roadside garbage pose civic challenges in Lumding
pages.text: Society & Youth Roaming cattle and roadside garbage pose civic challenges in Lumding The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T06:06:13 The issue of freely roaming cattle on public roads in Lumding has become a growing concern, raising questions about road safety and civic management. Garbage scattered along the roadside further compounds the problem, highlighting sanitation concerns and the need for better civic oversight. pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Society & Youth Roaming cattle and roadside garbage pose civic challenges in Lumding The Assam Tribune 2026-10-04T06:06:13 The presence of large animals on roads poses risks to both motorists and pedestrians. Two-wheeler riders, in particular, may face sudden evasive maneuvers by cattle, increasing the likelihood of falls and injuries. Pedestrians also struggle when cattle block roadside passages or narrow sections of the road. Local citizens have expressed the need for municipal or local authorities to address the issue systematically. They suggest identifying areas where cattle frequently roam and checking whether existing rules are being violated. Coordination with animal welfare agencies may also be necessary to ensure that measures are implemented without harming the animals. A temporary solution, such as removing cattle from specific stretches, is not sufficient. Instead, a long-term approach involving recurring location identification, communication with animal owners, and enforcement of regulations could help resolve the underlying problem. The situation in Lumding emphasizes the importance of responsible animal ownership and consistent civic oversight. Public roads must remain accessible to all users, while regular maintenance of roadside areas is essential to prevent waste accumulation. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/assam/roaming-cattle-roadside-garbage-raise-civic-concerns-in-lumding-1619279 29

The Assam Tribune 2026-10-01T12:34:04 Guwahati’s recent ODI between India and West Indies produced a record-breaking 811-run aggregate, featuring five centuries, a double hundred, and a dramatic 43.3-over chase—yet the match left many questioning whether the pitch truly delivered a balanced contest. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/opinion/guwahatis-800-run-odi-begs-a-simple-question-what-is-a-good-pitch-1619044 33

pages.text:
Continued
                
                    — Part 2 Sports & Achievements Guwahati’s 800-Run ODI: Did the Pitch Serve Cricket’s Core? The Assam Tribune 2026-10-01T12:34:04 The game saw West Indies post 405 for seven, their highest ODI total, before India chased it down with eight wickets in hand. While the spectacle of 800-plus runs and multiple centuries dominated headlines, critics like India head coach Gautam Gambhir argued that the pitch failed to create a meaningful contest between bat and ball. "You talk about cricket, but this is not cricket, this is only batting," Gambhir told Star Sports after the match, emphasizing that a good ODI should test all three disciplines equally. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, however, celebrated the pitch’s batting-friendly nature, calling it "an absolute delight" on social media. His perspective reflects a growing debate: Should a pitch be judged by its ability to produce high scores, or by its capacity to challenge batters, bowlers, and fielders alike? India’s batting coach Sitanshu Kotak added another layer to the discussion, questioning whether modern batting standards—powered by fitness, technology, and aggressive strokeplay—should influence pitch expectations. He noted that no pitch can guarantee a specific outcome, but the Guwahati surface’s consistency in producing high totals (including India’s 373 in 2023 and a 322 chase in 2018) raises concerns about its balance. The core issue lies in whether the pitch rewarded skill across all aspects of the game or merely amplified batting dominance. If 400 runs no longer feel challenging and bowlers struggle to find traction, the surface may have lost its ability to create uncertainty—the very essence of cricket. The Guwahati ODI’s record books may shine, but the debate over what constitutes a "good" pitch remains unresolved. Source: The Assam Tribune https://assamtribune.com/opinion/guwahatis-800-run-odi-begs-a-simple-question-what-is-a-good-pitch-1619044 34
